content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. In confessióne beáti Martíni.
content.english: Ant. let us praise our God.

segments.t: Ant.
In confessióne beáti Martíni.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

segments.t: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius

veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. In confessióne beáti Martíni.

In confessióne beáti Martíni.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
content.english: This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph

content.latin: Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
content.english: Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness

content.latin: Hac die lætus méruit suprémos
content.english: On this feast day year by year receiveth

content.latin: Laudis honóres.
content.english: Merited honors.

content.latin: Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
content.english: Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,

content.latin: Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
content.english: Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.

content.latin: Donec humános animávit auræ
content.english: While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,

content.latin: Spíritus artus.
content.english: Quickened his being.

content.latin: Cuius ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
content.english: Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,

content.latin: Ægra quæ passim iacuére membra,
content.english: Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,

content.latin: Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
content.english: Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,

content.latin: Restituúntur.
content.english: At his petition.

content.latin: Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
content.english: Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,

content.latin: Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
content.english: Chanting his praises with devout affection,

content.latin: Ut piis eius précibus iuvémur
content.english: That in his merits we may have a portion,

content.latin: Omne per ævum.
content.english: Now and forever.

content.latin: Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
content.english: His be the glory, power and salvation,

content.latin: Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
content.english: Who over all things reigneth in the highest,

content.latin: Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
content.english: Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,

content.latin: Trinus et unus.
content.english: Onely and Trinal.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: Psalm 1 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 1

content.latin: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
content.english: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:

content.latin: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
content.english: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

segments.t: Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.

content.latin: 1:3 Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
content.english: 1:3 And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

segments.t: Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:

content.latin: 1:3 Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
content.english: 1:3 And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

segments.t: Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.

content.latin: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
content.english: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

segments.t: Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.

content.latin: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
content.english: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

segments.t: Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.

content.latin: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
content.english: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

segments.t: Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.

content.latin: Psalmus 2 [2]
content.english: Psalm 2 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 2

content.latin: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
content.english: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

segments.t: Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?

content.latin: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
content.english: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

segments.t: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.

content.latin: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
content.english: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

segments.t: Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.

content.latin: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
content.english: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.

content.latin: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
content.english: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

segments.t: Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.

content.latin: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

segments.t: Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.

content.latin: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
content.english: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

segments.t: Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.

content.latin: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

segments.t: Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.

content.latin: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
content.english: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

segments.t: Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.

content.latin: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
content.english: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

segments.t: Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.

content.latin: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
content.english: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

segments.t: Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.

content.latin: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
content.english: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

segments.t: Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.

content.latin: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
content.english: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

segments.t: Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.

content.english: Ant. Not * in the shelter of a buckler, nor of an helmet, but with the sign of the Cross will I pierce the hosts of the enemy.

segments.t: Ant.
Ego signo crucis, * non clípeo protéctus, aut gálea, hóstium cúneos penetrábo secúrus.

content.latin: Psalmus 3 [3]
content.english: Psalm 3 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 3

content.latin: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
content.english: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

segments.t: Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.

content.latin: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.
content.english: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

segments.t: Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.

content.latin: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
content.english: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.

content.latin: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
content.english: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

segments.t: Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.

content.latin: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
content.english: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

segments.t: Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.

content.latin: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
content.english: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

segments.t: Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.

content.latin: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
content.english: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

segments.t: Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.

content.latin: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.
content.english: 3:9 Salvation is of the Lord: * and thy blessing is upon thy people.

segments.t: Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.

content.english: Ant. I trust * in the Lord that at thy prayers my daughter shall be healed.

segments.t: Ant.

content.latin: Psalmus 4 [4]
content.english: Psalm 4 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 4

content.latin: 4:2 Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.
content.english: 4:2 When I called upon him, the God of my justice heard me: * when I was in distress, thou hast enlarged me.

segments.t: Cum invocárem exaudívit me Deus iustítiæ meæ: * in tribulatióne dilatásti mihi.

content.latin: 4:2 Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: 4:2 Have mercy on me: * and hear my prayer.

segments.t: Miserére mei, * et exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: 4:3 Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?
content.english: 4:3 O ye sons of men, how long will you be dull of heart? * Why do you love vanity, and seek after lying?

segments.t: Fílii hóminum, úsquequo gravi corde? * ut quid dilígitis vanitátem, et quǽritis mendácium?

content.latin: 4:4 Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.
content.english: 4:4 Know ye also that the Lord hath made his holy one wonderful: * the Lord will hear me when I shall cry unto him.

segments.t: Et scitóte quóniam mirificávit Dóminus sanctum suum: * Dóminus exáudiet me cum clamávero ad eum.

content.latin: 4:5 Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.
content.english: 4:5 Be ye angry, and sin not: * the things you say in your hearts, be sorry for them upon your beds.

segments.t: Irascímini, et nolíte peccáre: * quæ dícitis in córdibus vestris, in cubílibus vestris compungímini.

content.latin: 4:6 Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?
content.english: 4:6 Offer up the sacrifice of justice, and trust in the Lord: * many say, Who sheweth us good things?

segments.t: Sacrificáte sacrifícium iustítiæ, et speráte in Dómino. * Multi dicunt: Quis osténdit nobis bona?

content.latin: 4:7 Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.
content.english: 4:7 The light of thy countenance, O Lord, is signed upon us: * thou hast given gladness in my heart.

segments.t: Signátum est super nos lumen vultus tui, Dómine: * dedísti lætítiam in corde meo.

content.latin: 4:8 A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.
content.english: 4:8 By the fruit of their corn, their wine, and oil, * they are multiplied.

segments.t: A fructu fruménti, vini, et ólei sui * multiplicáti sunt.

content.latin: 4:9 In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;
content.english: 4:9 In peace in the selfsame * I will sleep, and I will rest:

segments.t: In pace in idípsum * dórmiam, et requiéscam;

content.latin: 4:10 Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.
content.english: 4:10 For thou, O Lord, singularly * hast settled me in hope.

segments.t: Quóniam tu, Dómine, singuláriter in spe * constituísti me.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Confído in Dómino quod fília mea, précibus tuis, reddénda sit sanitáti.
content.english: Ant. I trust in the Lord that at thy prayers my daughter shall be healed.

segments.t: Ant.
Confído in Dómino quod fília mea, précibus tuis, reddénda sit sanitáti.

content.latin: Ant. Tetrádius, * cógnita Dei virtúte, ad baptísmi grátiam pervénit.
content.english: Ant. When Tetradius * knew the power of God, he attained unto the grace of baptism.

segments.t: Ant.
Tetrádius, * cógnita Dei virtúte, ad baptísmi grátiam pervénit.

content.latin: Psalmus 5 [5]
content.english: Psalm 5 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 5

content.latin: 5:2 Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.
content.english: 5:2 Give ear, O Lord, to my words * understand my cry.

segments.t: Verba mea áuribus pércipe, Dómine, * intéllege clamórem meum.

content.latin: 5:3 Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.
content.english: 5:3 Hearken to the voice of my prayer, * O my King and my God.

segments.t: Inténde voci oratiónis meæ, * Rex meus et Deus meus.

content.latin: 5:4 Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.
content.english: 5:4 For to thee will I pray: * O Lord, in the morning thou shalt hear my voice.

segments.t: Quóniam ad te orábo: * Dómine, mane exáudies vocem meam.

content.latin: 5:5 Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.
content.english: 5:5 In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see: * because thou art not a God that willest iniquity.

segments.t: Mane astábo tibi et vidébo: * quóniam non Deus volens iniquitátem tu es.

content.latin: 5:6 Neque habitábit iuxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt iniústi ante óculos tuos.
content.english: 5:6 Neither shall the wicked dwell near thee: * nor shall the unjust abide before thy eyes.

segments.t: Neque habitábit iuxta te malígnus: * neque permanébunt iniústi ante óculos tuos.

content.latin: 5:7 Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.
content.english: 5:7 Thou hatest all the workers of iniquity: * thou wilt destroy all that speak a lie.

segments.t: Odísti omnes, qui operántur iniquitátem: * perdes omnes, qui loquúntur mendácium.

content.latin: 5:7 Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.
content.english: 5:7 The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor. * But as for me in the multitude of thy mercy,

segments.t: Virum sánguinum et dolósum abominábitur Dóminus: * ego autem in multitúdine misericórdiæ tuæ.

content.latin: 5:8 Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.
content.english: 5:8 I will come into thy house; * I will worship towards thy holy temple, in thy fear.

segments.t: Introíbo in domum tuam: * adorábo ad templum sanctum tuum in timóre tuo.

content.latin: 5:9 Dómine, deduc me in iustítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.
content.english: 5:9 Conduct me, O Lord, in thy justice: * because of my enemies, direct my way in thy sight.

segments.t: Dómine, deduc me in iustítia tua: * propter inimícos meos dírige in conspéctu tuo viam meam.

content.latin: 5:10 Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.
content.english: 5:10 For there is no truth in their mouth: * their heart is vain.

segments.t: Quóniam non est in ore eórum véritas: * cor eórum vanum est.

content.latin: 5:11 Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, linguis suis dolóse agébant, * iúdica illos, Deus.
content.english: 5:11 Their throat is an open sepulchre: they dealt deceitfully with their tongues: * judge them, O God.

segments.t: Sepúlcrum patens est guttur eórum, linguis suis dolóse agébant, * iúdica illos, Deus.

content.latin: 5:11 Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.
content.english: 5:11 Let them fall from their devices: according to the multitude of their wickednesses cast them out: * for they have provoked thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Décidant a cogitatiónibus suis, secúndum multitúdinem impietátum eórum expélle eos, * quóniam irritavérunt te, Dómine.

content.latin: 5:12 Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.
content.english: 5:12 But let all them be glad that hope in thee: * they shall rejoice for ever, and thou shalt dwell in them.

segments.t: Et læténtur omnes, qui sperant in te, * in ætérnum exsultábunt: et habitábis in eis.

content.latin: 5:12 Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * quóniam tu benedíces iusto.
content.english: 5:12 And all they that love thy name shall glory in thee: * For thou wilt bless the just.

segments.t: Et gloriabúntur in te omnes, qui díligunt nomen tuum, * quóniam tu benedíces iusto.

content.latin: 5:13 Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.
content.english: 5:13 O Lord, thou hast crowned us, * as with a shield of thy good will.

segments.t: Dómine, ut scuto bonæ voluntátis tuæ * coronásti nos.

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: Ant. When Tetradius knew the power of God, he attained unto the grace of baptism.

segments.t: Ant.
Tetrádius, cógnita Dei virtúte, ad baptísmi grátiam pervénit.

content.latin: Ant. O ineffábilem virum, * per quem nobis tanta mirácula corúscant!
content.english: Ant. Not to be told * is this man's glory, by whom so many wonderful works have been set forth before us!

segments.t: Ant.
O ineffábilem virum, * per quem nobis tanta mirácula corúscant!

content.latin: Psalmus 8 [6]
content.english: Psalm 8 [6]

segments.t: Psalmus 8

content.latin: 8:2 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:2 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.latin: 8:2 Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.
content.english: 8:2 For thy magnificence is elevated * above the heavens.

segments.t: Quóniam eleváta est magnificéntia tua, * super cælos.

content.latin: 8:3 Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.
content.english: 8:3 Out of the mouth of infants and of sucklings thou hast perfected praise, because of thy enemies, * that thou mayst destroy the enemy and the avenger.

segments.t: Ex ore infántium et lacténtium perfecísti laudem propter inimícos tuos, * ut déstruas inimícum et ultórem.

content.latin: 8:4 Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.
content.english: 8:4 For I will behold thy heavens, the works of thy fingers: * the moon and the stars which thou hast founded.

segments.t: Quóniam vidébo cælos tuos, ópera digitórum tuórum: * lunam et stellas, quæ tu fundásti.

content.latin: 8:5 Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?
content.english: 8:5 What is man that thou art mindful of him? * or the son of man that thou visitest him?

segments.t: Quid est homo quod memor es eius? * aut fílius hóminis, quóniam vísitas eum?

content.latin: 8:6 Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.
content.english: 8:6 Thou hast made him a little less than the angels, thou hast crowned him with glory and honour: * and hast set him over the works of thy hands.

segments.t: Minuísti eum paulo minus ab Ángelis, glória et honóre coronásti eum: * et constituísti eum super ópera mánuum tuárum.

content.latin: 8:8 Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.
content.english: 8:8 Thou hast subjected all things under his feet, * all sheep and oxen: moreover the beasts also of the fields.

segments.t: Ómnia subiecísti sub pédibus eius, * oves et boves univérsas: ínsuper et pécora campi.

content.latin: 8:9 Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.
content.english: 8:9 The birds of the air, and the fishes of the sea, * that pass through the paths of the sea.

segments.t: Vólucres cæli, et pisces maris, * qui perámbulant sémitas maris.

content.latin: 8:10 Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!
content.english: 8:10 O Lord our Lord, * how admirable is thy name in all the earth!

segments.t: Dómine, Dóminus noster, * quam admirábile est nomen tuum in univérsa terra!

content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Ant. Not to be told is this man's glory, by whom so many wonderful works have been set forth before us!

segments.t: Ant.
O ineffábilem virum, per quem nobis tanta mirácula corúscant!

content.latin: Ant. Dóminus Iesus Christus, * non purpurátum aut diadémate reniténtem, se ventúrum esse prædíxit.
content.english: Ant. The Lord Jesus Christ * said not that He would come clothed in purple or adorned with a crown.

segments.t: Ant.
Dóminus Iesus Christus, * non purpurátum aut diadémate reniténtem, se ventúrum esse prædíxit.

content.latin: Psalmus 10 [7]
content.english: Psalm 10 [7]

segments.t: Psalmus 10

content.latin: 10:2 In Dómino confído: quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ: * Tránsmigra in montem sicut passer?
content.english: 10:2 In the Lord I put my trust: how then do you say to my soul: * Get thee away from hence to the mountain, like a sparrow?

segments.t: In Dómino confído: quómodo dícitis ánimæ meæ: * Tránsmigra in montem sicut passer?

content.latin: 10:3 Quóniam ecce peccatóres intendérunt arcum, paravérunt sagíttas suas in pháretra, * ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde.
content.english: 10:3 For, lo, the wicked have bent their bow: they have prepared their arrows in the quiver, * to shoot in the dark the upright of heart.

segments.t: Quóniam ecce peccatóres intendérunt arcum, paravérunt sagíttas suas in pháretra, * ut sagíttent in obscúro rectos corde.

content.latin: 10:4 Quóniam quæ perfecísti, destruxérunt: * iustus autem quid fecit?
content.english: 10:4 For they have destroyed the things which thou hast made: * but what has the just man done?

segments.t: Quóniam quæ perfecísti, destruxérunt: * iustus autem quid fecit?

content.latin: 10:5 Dóminus in templo sancto suo, * Dóminus in cælo sedes eius.
content.english: 10:5 The Lord is in his holy temple, * the Lord’s throne is in heaven.

segments.t: Dóminus in templo sancto suo, * Dóminus in cælo sedes eius.

content.latin: 10:5 Óculi eius in páuperem respíciunt: * pálpebræ eius intérrogant fílios hóminum.
content.english: 10:5 His eyes look on the poor man: * his eyelids examine the sons of men.

segments.t: Óculi eius in páuperem respíciunt: * pálpebræ eius intérrogant fílios hóminum.

content.latin: 10:6 Dóminus intérrogat iustum et ímpium: * qui autem díligit iniquitátem, odit ánimam suam.
content.english: 10:6 The Lord trieth the just and the wicked: * but he that loveth iniquity, hateth his own soul.

segments.t: Dóminus intérrogat iustum et ímpium: * qui autem díligit iniquitátem, odit ánimam suam.

content.latin: 10:7 Pluet super peccatóres láqueos: * ignis, et sulphur, et spíritus procellárum pars cálicis eórum.
content.english: 10:7 He shall rain snares upon sinners: * fire and brimstone, and storms of winds, shall be the portion of their cup.

segments.t: Pluet super peccatóres láqueos: * ignis, et sulphur, et spíritus procellárum pars cálicis eórum.

content.latin: 10:8 Quóniam iustus Dóminus, et iustítias diléxit: * æquitátem vidit vultus eius.
content.english: 10:8 For the Lord is just, and hath loved justice: * his countenance hath beheld righteousness.

segments.t: Quóniam iustus Dóminus, et iustítias diléxit: * æquitátem vidit vultus eius.

content.english: Ant. O Martin, * thou Priest of God, the heavens are open unto thee, yea, and the kingdom of My Father.

segments.t: Ant.
Sacérdos Dei, Martíne, * apérti sunt tibi cæli et regnum Patris mei.

content.latin: Psalmus 14 [8]
content.english: Psalm 14 [8]

segments.t: Psalmus 14

content.latin: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
content.english: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

segments.t: Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?

content.latin: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:
content.english: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

segments.t: Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:

content.latin: 14:3 Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
content.english: 14:3 He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

segments.t: Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:

content.latin: 14:3 Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
content.english: 14:3 Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

segments.t: Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.

content.latin: 14:4 Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
content.english: 14:4 In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

segments.t: Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:

content.latin: 14:4 Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
content.english: 14:4 He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

segments.t: Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.

content.latin: 14:5 Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
content.english: 14:5 He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

segments.t: Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

Sacérdos Dei, Martíne, apérti sunt tibi cæli et regnum Patris mei.

content.latin: Ant. Sacérdos Dei, Martíne, * pastor egrégie, ora pro nobis Deum.
content.english: Ant. O Martin, * thou Priest of God, thou worthy shepherd, pray God on our behalf.

segments.t: Ant.
Sacérdos Dei, Martíne, * pastor egrégie, ora pro nobis Deum.

content.latin: Psalmus 20 [9]
content.english: Psalm 20 [9]

segments.t: Psalmus 20

content.latin: 20:2 Dómine, in virtúte tua lætábitur rex: * et super salutáre tuum exsultábit veheménter.
content.english: 20:2 The king rejoices in thy strength, O Lord; * and in thy salvation he shall rejoice exceedingly.

segments.t: Dómine, in virtúte tua lætábitur rex: * et super salutáre tuum exsultábit veheménter.

content.latin: 20:3 Desidérium cordis eius tribuísti ei: * et voluntáte labiórum eius non fraudásti eum.
content.english: 20:3 Thou hast given him his heart’s desire: * and hast not withholden from him the will of his lips.

segments.t: Desidérium cordis eius tribuísti ei: * et voluntáte labiórum eius non fraudásti eum.

content.latin: 20:4 Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: * posuísti in cápite eius corónam de lápide pretióso.
content.english: 20:4 For thou hast prevented him with blessings of sweetness: * thou hast set on his head a crown of precious stones.

segments.t: Quóniam prævenísti eum in benedictiónibus dulcédinis: * posuísti in cápite eius corónam de lápide pretióso.

content.latin: 20:5 Vitam pétiit a te: * et tribuísti ei longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 20:5 He asked life of thee: * and thou hast given him length of days for ever and ever.

segments.t: Vitam pétiit a te: * et tribuísti ei longitúdinem diérum in sǽculum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 20:6 Magna est glória eius in salutári tuo: * glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.
content.english: 20:6 His glory is great in thy salvation: * glory and great beauty shalt thou lay upon him.

segments.t: Magna est glória eius in salutári tuo: * glóriam et magnum decórem impónes super eum.

content.latin: 20:7 Quóniam dabis eum in benedictiónem in sǽculum sǽculi: * lætificábis eum in gáudio cum vultu tuo.

content.latin: Martínus, Sabáriæ in Pannónia natus, cum décimum attigísset annum, invítis paréntibus ad ecclésiam confúgiens, in catechumenórum númerum adscríbi vóluit. Aduléscens quíndecim annórum in milítiam proféctus, primum in Constántii, deínde Iuliáni exércitu militávit. Decem et octo annos natus, cum Ambiáni partem clámydis cuídam páuperi donásset, mira exínde Iesu Christi apparitióne recreátus, álacri ánimo baptísmum suscépit; tum, relícta militári vita, ab Hilário Pictaviénsi epíscopo in acolythórum númerum est recéptus. Póstea factus epíscopus Turonénsis, monastérium ædificávit, ubi cum octogínta mónachis sanctíssime aliquámdiu vixit. Qui, cum ad Candacénsem vicum suæ diœcésis in gravem febrim incidísset, suórum miserátus discipulórum, sic Deum rogábat: Dómine, si adhuc pópulo tuo sum necessárius, non recúso labórem. Mox instánte iam morte, viso humáni géneris hoste, Quid, inquit, astas, cruénta béstia? nihil in me funéste repéries. Ea in voce, unum et octogínta annos natus, multis miráculis gloriósus, ánimam Deo réddidit.
content.english: Martin, born in Sabaria at Pannonia, was ten years old, when against his parents' wishes he went to a Church and asked to be enrolled amongst the catechumens. At fifteen he enlisted as a soldier, and served first in the army of Constantius, and then in that of Julian. At eighteen, when he had given part of his cloak to a poor man at Amiens, he was strengthened by a wonderful apparition of Jesus Christ and eagerly received baptism. Then leaving the military life, he was received among the acolytes of Hilary, the bishop of Poitiers. Later made bishop of Tours, he built a monastery, where with eighty monks he lived in a most holy way for some time. When he was seized with severe fever at Candes, a village of his diocese, he had pity on his disciples, and thus prayed to God: “Lord, if I am still necessary for your people, I will not refuse the labor.” Shortly after, when death was imminent, the enemy of mankind appeared him. “Why are you here, cruel beast?”, said Martin. “You will find no deadly sin in me.” With those words he gave back his soul to God at the age of eighty one, famous for many miracles.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

segments.t: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem
Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

segments.t: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, qui cónspicis, quia ex nulla nostra virtúte subsístimus: concéde propítius; ut, intercessióne beáti Martíni Confessóris tui atque Pontíficis, contra ómnia advérsa muniámur.
content.english: Grant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that the worshipful Feast of thy blessed Confessor and Bishop Martin, may avail us to the increase both of godliness toward thee, and healthfulness to our own souls.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.english: Ant. His disciples said * unto Blessed Martin: Father, why wilt thou go away from us? or with whom wilt thou leave us orphans? For ravening wolves will break in upon thy flock.

content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

segments.t: Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

segments.t: Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.

content.latin: 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.
content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

segments.t: Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: * the floods have lifted up their voice.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up their waves, * with the noise of many waters.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.

content.latin: 92:4 Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.
content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

segments.t: Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.

content.latin: 92:5 Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

segments.t: Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.

segments.t: Ant.
Dómine, * si adhuc pópulo tuo sum necessárius, non recúso labórem: fiat volúntas tua.

content.latin: Psalmus 99 [2]
content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 99

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

segments.t: Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.

content.latin: 99:2 Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.
content.english: 99:2 Come in before his presence * with exceeding great joy.

segments.t: Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.

content.latin: 99:3 Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.
content.english: 99:3 Know ye that the Lord he is God: * he made us, and not we ourselves.

segments.t: Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.

content.latin: 99:3 Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.
content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

segments.t: Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

segments.t: Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 62

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.english: Canticle of the Three Young Men [4]

segments.t: Canticum Trium Puerorum

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.

content.english: 3:73 O ye spirits and souls of the just, bless the Lord: * O ye holy and humble of heart, bless the Lord.

content.latin: 148:1 Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.
content.english: 148:1 Praise ye the Lord from the heavens * praise ye him in the high places.

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de cælis: * laudáte eum in excélsis.

content.latin: 148:2 Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.
content.english: 148:2 Praise ye him, all his angels: * praise ye him, all his hosts.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, omnes Ángeli eius: * laudáte eum, omnes virtútes eius.

content.latin: 148:3 Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.
content.english: 148:3 Praise ye him, O sun and moon: * praise him, all ye stars and light.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, sol et luna: * laudáte eum, omnes stellæ et lumen.

content.latin: 148:4 Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.
content.english: 148:4 Praise him, ye heavens of heavens: * and let all the waters that are above the heavens, praise the name of the Lord.

segments.t: Laudáte eum, cæli cælórum: * et aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, laudent nomen Dómini.

content.latin: 148:5 Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.
content.english: 148:5 For he spoke, and they were made: * he commanded, and they were created.

segments.t: Quia ipse dixit, et facta sunt: * ipse mandávit, et creáta sunt.

content.latin: 148:6 Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.
content.english: 148:6 He hath established them for ever, and for ages of ages: * he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away.

segments.t: Státuit ea in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi: * præcéptum pósuit, et non præteríbit.

content.latin: 148:7 Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.
content.english: 148:7 Praise the Lord from the earth, * ye dragons, and all ye deeps:

segments.t: Laudáte Dóminum de terra, * dracónes, et omnes abýssi.

content.latin: 148:8 Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:
content.english: 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds * which fulfill his word:

segments.t: Ignis, grando, nix, glácies, spíritus procellárum: * quæ fáciunt verbum eius:

content.latin: 148:9 Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.
content.english: 148:9 Mountains and all hills, * fruitful trees and all cedars:

segments.t: Montes, et omnes colles: * ligna fructífera, et omnes cedri.

content.latin: 148:10 Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:
content.english: 148:10 Beasts and all cattle: * serpents and feathered fowls:

segments.t: Béstiæ, et univérsa pécora: * serpéntes, et vólucres pennátæ:

content.latin: 148:11 Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.
content.english: 148:11 Kings of the earth and all people: * princes and all judges of the earth:

segments.t: Reges terræ, et omnes pópuli: * príncipes, et omnes iúdices terræ.

content.latin: 148:12 Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.
content.english: 148:12 Young men and maidens: let the old with the younger, praise the name of the Lord: * For his name alone is exalted.

segments.t: Iúvenes, et vírgines: senes cum iunióribus laudent nomen Dómini: * quia exaltátum est nomen eius solíus.

content.latin: 148:14 Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.
content.english: 148:14 The praise of him is above heaven and earth: * and he hath exalted the horn of his people.

segments.t: Conféssio eius super cælum et terram: * et exaltávit cornu pópuli sui.

segments.t: Hymnus ómnibus sanctis eius: * fíliis Israël, pópulo appropinquánti sibi.

content.latin: Qui rite mundi gáudia

content.latin: Huius cadúca réspuens,
content.english: As vain and passing, he eschewed;

content.english: And therefore with angelic bands,

content.latin: Huius benígnus ánnue
content.english: Grant then that we, most gracious God,

segments.t: Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

segments.t: Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.

content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

segments.t: Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:

segments.t: Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

segments.t: Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

segments.t: In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;

segments.t: Psalmus 25

content.latin: 25:1 Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
content.english: 25:1 Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.

segments.t: Iúdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.

content.latin: 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
content.english: 25:2 Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.

segments.t: Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.

content.latin: 25:3 Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
content.english: 25:3 For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.

segments.t: Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.

content.latin: 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
content.english: 25:4 I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.

segments.t: Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.

content.latin: 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
content.english: 25:5 I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.

segments.t: Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.

content.latin: 25:6 Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
content.english: 25:6 I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:

segments.t: Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:

content.latin: 25:7 Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
content.english: 25:7 That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.

segments.t: Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.

content.latin: 25:8 Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
content.english: 25:8 I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.

segments.t: Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.

content.latin: 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
content.english: 25:9 Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:

segments.t: Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:

content.latin: 25:10 In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
content.english: 25:10 In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.

segments.t: In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.

content.latin: 25:11 Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
content.english: 25:11 But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.

segments.t: Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.

content.latin: 25:12 Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
content.english: 25:12 My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.

segments.t: Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.

content.latin: Psalmus 51 [2]
content.english: Psalm 51 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 51

content.latin: 51:3 Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
content.english: 51:3 Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?

segments.t: Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?

content.latin: 51:4 Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
content.english: 51:4 All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

segments.t: Tota die iniustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.

content.latin: 51:5 Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
content.english: 51:5 Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

segments.t: Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.

content.latin: 51:6 Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
content.english: 51:6 Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.

segments.t: Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.

content.latin: 51:7 Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
content.english: 51:7 Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

segments.t: Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.

content.latin: 51:8 Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:
content.english: 51:8 The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:

segments.t: Vidébunt iusti, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adiutórem suum:

content.latin: 51:9 Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
content.english: 51:9 But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.

segments.t: Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.

content.latin: 51:10 Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: 51:10 But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.

segments.t: Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: 51:11 Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
content.english: 51:11 I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.

segments.t: Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.

content.latin: 52:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
content.english: 52:1 The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.

segments.t: Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.

content.latin: 52:2 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
content.english: 52:2 They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.

segments.t: Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.

content.latin: 52:3 Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
content.english: 52:3 God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.

segments.t: Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.

content.latin: 52:4 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
content.english: 52:4 All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.

segments.t: Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.

content.latin: 52:5 Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
content.english: 52:5 Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?

segments.t: Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?

content.latin: 52:6 Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
content.english: 52:6 They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

segments.t: Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.

content.latin: 52:6 Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
content.english: 52:6 For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.

segments.t: Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.

content.latin: 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.
content.english: 52:7 Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

segments.t: Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Iacob, et lætábitur Israël.

content.latin: Dómine Deus omnípotens, qui ad princípium huius diéi nos perveníre fecísti: tua nos hódie salva virtúte; ut in hac die ad nullum declinémus peccátum, sed semper ad tuam iustítiam faciéndam nostra procédant elóquia, dirigántur cogitatiónes et ópera.
content.english: O Lord, our heavenly Father, Almighty and everlasting God, who has safely brought us to the beginning of this day: defend us by thy mighty power; and grant that this day we fall into no sin, but that all our doings may be ordered by thy governance, to do always what is righteous in thy sight.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

content.english: November 12th 2026, the 2nd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:

content.latin: Sancti Martíni Primi, Papæ et Mártyris, cuius dies natális sextodécimo Kaléndas Octóbris recensétur.
content.english: The holy martyr, Pope Martin. He got together a synod at Rome, wherein he condemned the heretics Sergius, Paul, and Pyrrhus. Wherefore the heretic Emperor Constans caused him to be kidnapped and brought to Constantinople, whence he was banished into the Crimea, where he died, (in the year 655,) worn out by his sufferings for the Catholic faith's sake. He was famous for miracles. His body was afterward brought to Rome and buried in the Church of SS. Sylvester and Martin.

content.latin: Vitépsci, in Polónia, pássio sancti Iósaphat, e sancti Basilíi Ordine, Epíscopi Polocénsis et Mártyris; qui a schismáticis, in ódium cathólicæ unitátis et veritátis, crudéliter interféctus est, et a Pio Papa Nono inter sanctos Mártyres adscríptus. Eius tamen festívitas recólitur décimo octávo Kaléndas Decémbris.
content.english: In Asia, the holy martyrs and Bishops Aurelius and Publius.

content.latin: Complúti, in Hispánia, natális sancti Dídaci Confessóris, ex Ordine Minórum, humilitáte célebris; quem Xystus Quintus, Póntifex Máximus, Sanctórum catálogo adscrípsit. Ipsíus autem festum sequénti die celebrátur.
content.english: In the country of Sens, (in the year 726,) the holy martyr Paternus.

content.latin: In Asia pássio sanctórum Aurélii et Públii Episcopórum.
content.english: At Gent, the holy martyr Livin, Bishop (in Ireland, Apostle of West Flanders, martyred at Esse, in Belgium, in the seventh century.)

content.latin: Eschæ, in Bélgio, sancti Livíni, Epíscopi et Mártyris; qui, cum plúrimos ad Christi fidem convertísset, a Pagánis necátus est. Ipsíus vero corpus ad Portum Gandæ póstea translátum fuit.
content.english: In Poland, the holy martyred Hermits Benedict, John, Matthew, Isaac, and Christinus.

content.latin: Apud Casimíriam, in Polónia, sanctórum Mártyrum Eremitárum Benedícti, Ioánnis, Matthǽi, Isaac et Christiáni; qui a prædónibus, divíno inténti servítio, dire vexáti sunt et gládiis occísi.
content.english: At Vitepsk, in Poland, the holy martyr Jehosaphat, Archbishop of Polotsk, Monk of the Order of St. Basil, who was cruelly murdered by schismatics, (in the year 1623,) out of their hatred for Catholic unity and truth, and whose name Pope Pius IX enrolled among those of the holy martyrs. We keep his feast upon the 28th day of this present month of November.

content.latin: Apud óppidum Sergíniam, in território Senonénsi, sancti Patérni, Mónachi et Mártyris; qui, dum eídem occurréntes in ipsíus óppidi silva latrónes ad emendándam vitam incitáret, ab illis trucidátus est.
content.english: At Avignon, holy Rufus, the first Bishop of that see.

content.latin: Avenióne sancti Rufi, qui éxstitit primus eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
content.english: At Cologne, (in the year 663,) holy Cunibert, Bishop (of that see.)

content.latin: Colóniæ Agrippínæ deposítio sancti Cunibérti Epíscopi.
content.english: At Tarragona, in Spain, the blessed Priest Emilian, who was famous for countless miracles, and whose wonderful life hath been written by Braulio, the holy Bishop of Zaragoza.

content.latin: Turiasóne, in Hispánia Tarraconénsi, beáti Æmiliáni Presbýteri, qui innúmeris miráculis cláruit; cuius admirábilem vitam sanctus Bráulio, Cæsaraugustánus Epíscopus, descrípsit.
content.english: At Constantinople, the holy Abbot Nilus, who had been Prefect of the city, but became a Monk, and was famous for teaching and holiness in the time of the Emperor Theodosius the younger.

content.latin: Constantinópoli sancti Nili Abbátis, qui, sub Theodósio iunióre, ex Præfécto eiúsdem civitátis factus Mónachus, doctrína et sanctitáte cláruit.
content.english: Likewise at Constantinople, holy Theodore, of the monastery which is called the Studium who contended mightily for the Catholic faith against the Iconoclasts, and became famous throughout the whole Catholic Church, (a.d. 759-826.)

content.latin: ℣. Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
content.english: At Alcala, in Spain, (in the year 1463,) the holy Confessor Diego, of the Order of Friars Minor, eminent for his lowliness, whose name Sixtus V enrolled among those of the Saints, and whose feast is kept upon the morrow after.

segments.t: Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.

content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.latin: ℣. Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.
content.english: ℣. Look upon thy servants and upon thy works: and direct their children.

segments.t: Réspice in servos tuos, Dómine, et in ópera tua, et dírige fílios eórum.

content.latin: ℟. Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.
content.english: ℟. And let the brightness of the Lord our God be upon us. Direct thou the works of our hands; yea, the work of our hands do thou direct.

segments.t: Et sit splendor Dómini Dei nostri super nos, et ópera mánuum nostrárum dírige super nos, et opus mánuum nostrárum dírige.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Dirígere et sanctificáre, régere et gubernáre dignáre, Dómine Deus, Rex cæli et terræ, hódie corda et córpora nostra, sensus, sermónes et actus nostros in lege tua, et in opéribus mandatórum tuórum: ut hic et in ætérnum, te auxiliánte, salvi et líberi esse mereámur, Salvátor mundi: Qui vivis et regnas in sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: O Lord, Almighty God, King of heaven and earth, Saviour of the world, bless, lead, rule and govern our hearts and bodies, our senses, words and deeds today, following thy law and commandments, that here and for eternity with thy help we shall be saved in freedom. Who livest and reignest, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: And the Lord direct your hearts, in the charity of God, and the patience of Christ.

content.english: Benediction. May the Lord bless us, ✠ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.english: Psalm 53 [1]

content.latin: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.
content.english: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

segments.t: Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua iúdica me.

content.latin: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
content.english: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

segments.t: Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.

content.latin: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
content.english: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

segments.t: Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.

content.latin: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
content.english: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

segments.t: Ecce enim, Deus ádiuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.

content.latin: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
content.english: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

segments.t: Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.

content.latin: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
content.english: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

segments.t: Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:

content.latin: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
content.english: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

segments.t: Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
